title: accept_large_sparse=False breaks under sparse_interface="sparray" because sparse arrays keep int64 indices
answers: SpectralEmbedding raises ValueError about 64-bit sparse indices with sparray
when should I pass accept_large_sparse=False to check_array
kneighbors_graph returns int64 indices with csr_array
body:
Symptom: SpectralEmbedding / SpectralClustering (default eigen_solver="arpack") raised a ValueError about 64-bit sparse indices when fitted under config_context(sparse_interface="sparray"), even on small data.
Root cause: sklearn/manifold/_spectral_embedding.py:_spectral_embedding called check_array(laplacian, accept_sparse="csr", accept_large_sparse=False) in the arpack branch. scipy sparse arrays (csr_array, unlike csr_matrix) never downcast index dtype by content when built from (data, indices, indptr) (scipy/scipy#16774), so the kneighbors_graph output, 0.5*(A+A.T) and csgraph laplacian all carry int64 indices.
Fix pattern: drop accept_large_sparse=False (default True) when the consumer is pure scipy (eigsh, incl. shift-invert sigma=-1e-5, handles int64 indices), matching the amg/lobpcg branches of the same function.
Constraints: keep accept_large_sparse=False only where the data goes into Cython/C code needing 32-bit index buffers (libsvm, liblinear, k-means _k_means_lloyd, coordinate descent, SGD per the PR); those estimators still reject int64-indexed sparray input by design. Any new accept_large_sparse=False guard should be checked against sparray input, since index size there doesn't track the data size.
applies: Any check_array/validate_data call on sparse input that may come from scipy sparse arrays (sparse_interface="sparray"), especially graph/kNN-derived matrices
